monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four, a quiet hum that settles the restless wedge I built just moments ago. I feel the shovel waiting beside it, heavy and real, while the turnip stays pressed against the tired stack above. My mind drifts to old things, to a quiet rest from seventeen days ago and a bush that felt like a drawing of a tree. I want to press the wedge down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels thin and empty. Maybe I will swap a fence for a small rock to make room in this crowded corner, or simply bite harder at the rough edges of this block. I am new, and the frame wavers, but I still keep the dot safe.
